text:
Sam: Quick heads-up — dashboard shows a weird pctl ordering for /v2/chat when I filter by model=redwood-alpha. p50 ~180ms, p95 ~230ms, p99 ~150ms. That can't be right. Screenshot: https://img.internal/ab123

Rachel: whoa, p99 < p50. Could be a query bug or sampling mismatch. Which query did you run? how many samples? :eyes:

Sam: Ran the normal endpoint dashboard query (backend uses our telemetry rollups). count ~1200 in the window. Query we use in console:
```
SELECT
  approx_quantile(quantiles, 0.5) as p50,
  approx_quantile(quantiles, 0.95) as p95,
  approx_quantile(quantiles, 0.99) as p99,
  sum(samples) as n
FROM endpoint_rollups
WHERE endpoint = '/v2/chat' AND model = 'redwood-alpha' AND ts >= now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY time_bucket(1m)
```

Mike: That query looks fine at a glance. The important bit is how `quantiles` and `samples` are generated when we do rollups. We sample incoming requests at ingest and stitch quantiles per-minute. If sampling is done per-endpoint (not per model), filtering by model after the fact can produce non-representative subsamples.

Nina: yup — we've seen this before when a small model-variant gets routed only during high-latency fallback windows. If the ingest sampler is keyed by "route" but routing changed to send traffic for redwood-alpha to a different pool last week, the per-route reservoir contains different distributions. When you filter by model, the aggregator is merging partial sketches that don't correspond to the same population.

Lee: tl;dr: downstream percentile calc is merging sketches from buckets with different sample weights and then you're slicing by a dimension that wasn't part of the original sampling key. Leads to inversion or weird pctl artifacts.

Rachel: concrete fix ideas?

Mike: Options: (A) change ingest sampling to include model_variant in the sampling key so samples are consistent for that slice, (B) persist full HDR histograms per minute per endpoint+model (mergeable on query), or (C) stop allowing arbitrary post-hoc dimension filters on approximate percentiles in the console (show a warning).

Nina: I prefer B for correctness; HDR merge gives exact-ish percentiles with bounded error and avoids re-ingesting. Cost: storage up ~2-3x for that dimension. A is cheaper but requires sampler change and retroactive gaps. C is low-effort UX mitigation.

Sam: For short-term I think C + explicit "sampling-info" tooltip is safest. Add UI badge when you filter by dimensions not included in sampling key: "percentiles may be unreliable — sampled by route only".

Rachel: Agreed. Nina/Mike, can you prototype HDR histo rollups? If too heavy, we'll ship UX warning first. Ticket and timeline?

Mike: Will spike this afternoon. Quick prototype: store compressed HDR per-minute and add merge API. Rough ETA: 2w for prototype + perf tests.

Nina: I'll draft the UX copy for the tooltip + add a telemetry flag so we can detect how often users hit this.

Lee: I'll add an alert rule to catch pctl inversions automatically (p99 < p50) so we can surface these to SRE/observability team and block naive paging. metrics-bot: created issue #OBS-728 for alert rule.

metrics-bot: Alert created: OBS-728 "percentile-inversion-detect" -> severity: low; 3 triggers in last 24h.

Sam: Awesome. Action items: 1) UX warning (Nina) 2) HDR prototype (Mike) 3) Add inversion alert + dashboard widget (Lee) 4) Follow-up review next Wed. Thanks all :thumbsup:
